output.title: Show HN: depsentry – Behavioral dependency scanner for npm and PyPI
output.body:
depsentry watches what dependencies do, not just what CVE databases say. It flags new install scripts, sudden maintainer handoffs, typosquat-adjacent names, obfuscated payloads, and network calls added in minor versions—the behavioral signals that preceded attacks like event-stream.

It runs in CI, scans a 1,200-dependency lockfile in about 40 seconds, and comments directly on the PR that introduces a risky dependency. Our retro-analysis shows it would have flagged the event-stream/flatmap-stream attack 11 days before public disclosure.

Built in Rust for performance, with GitHub Actions integration. Free for open-source repos; team plan at $199/month. Currently supports npm and PyPI, with GitLab support in development.

Would love feedback on detection accuracy, false positive rate, and integration depth from security and platform engineers.
